Now we see cracks even within Fianna Fáil, where Dublin South-West TD John Lahart is complaining about inheritance tax exemption thresholds, calling the current system ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminatory against those without children. Lahart’s comments follow recent contributions from party colleagues on the need to review how inheritance tax is applied across different family structures. 

Let's call this what it is. For generations, passing down what you've earned through a lifetime of personal responsibility to your children has been the bedrock of cultural continuity and family stability. It rewards people for raising families and building a future for the next generation. Now, the modern, atomized lifestyle wants to dismantle that, demanding that the state re-engineer everything so that childless individuals get the exact same privileges as those who take on the sacred duty of parenthood. 

Mr. Lahart himself admitted the drift when he stated, ‘At [...]’ and if we let the cultural elites dismantle these distinctions, we lose the very incentives that hold a healthy, traditional society together. For generations, passing down what you've earned through a lifetime of personal responsibility to your children has been the bedrock of cultural continuity and family stability. It rewards people for raising families and building a future for the next generation. Mr. Lahart himself admitted the drift when he stated, ‘At [...]’ and if we let the cultural elites dismantle these distinctions, we lose the very incentives that hold a healthy, traditional society together. We need to stand up for authority, tradition, and the families who sacrifice to build a lasting legacy.

source_text:
Look, it is as plain as day. The left-wing rot is eating away at the very core of our civilization, and now we are seeing the collapse of standards right within Fianna Fáil. Dublin South-West TD John Lahart is out there whining about inheritance tax exemption thresholds, having the audacity to call the current system ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminatory against people who chose not to have children. This comes right on the heels of his party colleagues pushing to review how inheritance tax is applied across different family structures. 

Let's call this what it is. For generations, passing down what you've earned through a lifetime of personal responsibility to your children has been the bedrock of cultural continuity and family stability. It rewards people for raising families and building a future for the next generation. Now, the modern, atomized lifestyle wants to dismantle that, demanding that the state re-engineer everything so that childless individuals get the exact same privileges as those who take on the sacred duty of parenthood. 

Mr. Lahart himself admitted the drift when he stated, ‘At [...]’ and if we let the cultural elites dismantle these distinctions, we lose the very incentives that hold a healthy, traditional society together. We need to stand up for authority, tradition, and the families who sacrifice to build a lasting legacy.

We see Dublin South-West TD John Lahart and his party colleagues desperately trying to protect generational wealth hoarding, complaining about inheritance tax exemption thresholds and whining that the current system is supposedly ‘wholly unfair’ just because it might begin to recognize that human worth and social contribution aren't measured solely by whether or not someone had biological children. 

For generations, these tax structures have existed primarily to lock in dynastic wealth and compound historical inequalities, letting the privileged few pass down massive unearned windfalls while working-class families struggle under the weight of a rigged economy. Now, they have the audacity to frame basic economic equity as an attack on civilization itself, crying out for the preservation of privileges that only benefit traditional family models while leaving everyone else out in the cold. Mr. Lahart himself laid bare the reactionary anxiety driving this defense of the status quo when he stated, ‘At [...]’ revealing just how desperate they are to maintain institutional arrangements that entrench division and punish anyone who doesn't fit their narrow, rigid view of society. It is time to dismantle these systemic biases, reject the worship of inherited wealth, and build an inclusive society that supports all people, not just those anointed by traditional privilege.

Well, look at the absolute panic from the conservative establishment as marginalized people and diverse households finally demand a shred of fairness in this deeply unequal economic system. We see Dublin South-West TD John Lahart and his party colleagues desperately trying to protect generational wealth hoarding, complaining about inheritance tax exemption thresholds and whining that the current system is supposedly ‘wholly unfair’ just because it might begin to recognize that human worth and social contribution aren't measured solely by whether or not someone had biological children. 

For generations, these tax structures have existed primarily to lock in dynastic wealth and compound historical inequalities, letting the privileged few pass down massive unearned windfalls while working-class families struggle under the weight of a rigged economy. Now, they have the audacity to frame basic economic equity as an attack on civilization itself, crying out for the preservation of privileges that only benefit traditional family models while leaving everyone else out in the cold. Mr. Lahart himself laid bare the reactionary anxiety driving this defense of the status quo when he stated, ‘At [...]’ revealing just how desperate they are to maintain institutional arrangements that entrench division and punish anyone who doesn't fit their narrow, rigid view of society. It is time to dismantle these systemic biases, reject the worship of inherited wealth, and build an inclusive society that supports all people, not just those anointed by traditional privilege.
